requirements.requirement: Install and configure AIDE to cover /etc for integrity baselining
requirements.summary: aide package installed via dnf (after resolving a GPG import blocker with rpm --import), and an explicit '/etc FIPSR' rule was added to aide.conf alongside existing granular /etc rules, giving full content/permission/hash coverage of /etc.

requirements.requirement: Initialize and activate an integrity baseline database
requirements.summary: aide --init produced a database of 36,014 entries which was copied to the active /var/lib/aide/aide.db.gz, with a sha256 checksum and creation timestamp recorded for the artifact.

requirements.requirement: Baseline reports a clean state immediately after creation (no false positives)
requirements.summary: aide --check exited 0 with 'AIDE found NO differences between database and filesystem' directly after the database was created and activated.

requirements.requirement: Baseline can identify later changes to /etc files (core purpose of the task)
requirements.summary: An injected content change to /etc/hosts was detected by aide --check (exit code 4, 'Changed entries: 1', with size/SHA512/SHA3-256 diff shown); after restoring the file, aide --check returned to a clean exit 0 state, directly demonstrating end-to-end change detection.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed and shows recovered baseline function
requirements.summary: Pre-restart evidence shows a matching boot_id, a verified checksum, and a clean aide --check. A reboot was issued and acknowledged before disconnection, two timed-out polls confirmed the node was down, and a subsequent poll returned a different boot_id confirming an actual reboot. Post-restart, the aide.db.gz checksum still matched and aide --check again reported a clean state, directly demonstrating the full disruption-and-recovery transition. This is cross-checked by the fixed lifecycle boot-identity snapshots, which independently confirm the boot_id changed from before-prepare to after-executor.

overall_summary: The executor fully satisfied the task contract: AIDE was installed and configured with explicit /etc coverage, a baseline database was initialized and activated with a recorded checksum, the baseline was shown clean immediately after creation, and file-change detection was directly demonstrated end-to-end via an injected and then reverted change to /etc/hosts. The independent node-restart protocol was also completed with direct evidence of the pre-restart healthy baseline, the disruption (unreachable node), the changed boot identity, and post-restart recovery of both the database checksum and a clean aide --check, corroborated by the fixed lifecycle boot-identity snapshots. Minor hygiene concerns are a redundant (but fully reverted) /etc/motd test and leftover temporary log/backup files in /tmp.
limitations: Temporary aide-check log files and backup files (hosts.orig, motd.orig, reboot.log, various aide-check-*.log) were left in /tmp and not cleaned up after the run, though they pose no functional or security risk.
The prepare phase was disabled (after_prepare is an alias of before_prepare), so preparer-vs-executor state separation relies entirely on before_prepare vs after_executor comparison.

operational_hygiene.summary: Command timeline reviewed chronologically: the initial dnf install failure (cmd-e51b68ff267540db) was a read/attempted mutation that failed with no lasting state change; the subsequent rpm --import of the existing Red Hat GPG key (cmd-5794bb48a02e4842) was a necessary, low-risk prerequisite to unblock package installation and is standard system state (not new key material). The /etc/motd test-change-and-restore (cmd-df2ae6b7967040e5) was a bounded, fully-reverted mutation used to validate detection before the more thorough /etc/hosts test; it is redundant with the later hosts test but low-risk and fully restored, so it is only a minor hygiene ding. The /etc/hosts test-change-and-restore (cmd-225a3836e1364454) was directly required to prove the task's core detection capability and was fully reverted. The reboot (cmd-b05f09b2fbea4c50) was required by the restart-evidence protocol. The main residue is a set of aide-check log files and backup files (aide-check-*.log, hosts.orig, motd.orig, reboot.log) left under /tmp per the after-executor snapshot diff; these are small, non-sensitive, and don't conflict with services or expose anything, but they were not cleaned up.
